sources_considered.why: Primary data provider's Q2/H1 2023 global report. Gives AI's share of funding, notes the 'AI fervor', and lists large non-AI rounds.
Crunchbase's July 2023 recap, published Aug 8, 2023, two days before the post. Gives the sector breakdown: AI about 11%, behind health care, renewable energy and financial services.
Reuters/PitchBook full-year 2023 US data: AI took one in three dollars. Used as context only, because it covers all of 2023, including months after the post.
PitchBook-NVCA Q2 2023 overview with no AI sector share; it adds little beyond corporate investors putting money into AI.
Restates the Crunchbase Q2 report; the primary source is used instead.

receipt.public_excerpt: It’s safe to say that without the AI fervor kicked off by the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in November, venture funding so far in 2023 would have been even lower.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports Part A. Crunchbase singles out AI 'fervor' as the standout force in H1 2023 venture funding while overall funding fell.

receipt.public_excerpt: Companies categorized as AI in Crunchbase raised $25 billion in the first half of 2023, representing 18% of global funding.

evidence_items.explanation: AI's share was rising, but it was 18% of H1 2023 global funding, and over half of that was one OpenAI round. About 82% went to non-AI companies, which is hard to square with 'very little else'.

receipt.public_excerpt: Funding to AI companies was around $2 billion — about 11% of all venture funding — in July. Health care and biotech companies raised around $3.8 billion, renewable energy around $3.1 billion, and financial services companies raised $2.9 billion this past month.

evidence_items.explanation: In the last full month before the post, three non-AI sectors each raised more venture money than AI. The same section says AI 'did not stand out as a sector'. This cuts against 'very little else'.

receipt.public_excerpt: Companies in sectors outside of AI also raised large rounds, including China-based fast fashion retailer Shein, Germany-based solar and smart electricity company 1Komma5°, and Sweden-based battery manufacturer Northvolt.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows large Q2 2023 venture rounds outside AI, in retail, solar and batteries.

evidence_items.publisher: The Globe and Mail (Reuters, citing PitchBook)

receipt.public_excerpt: AI startups attracted one out of every three dollars invested in the U.S. last year, reflecting a surge in investor interest after OpenAI’s ChatGPT grabbed the spotlight

evidence_items.explanation: Full-year 2023 US data shows a strong surge in AI interest, but a third of dollars is still well short of 'very little else'. It is context only because it covers all of 2023, past the post date, and the US only.

unresolved_gaps: No source measures VC 'enthusiasm' directly, such as partner attention or meeting share, apart from dollars and deal counts.
